NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — To prevent creep and ozone-induced cracking in laminated elastomeric bridge bearing pads, we propose replacing the standard elastomer layers with a specially formulated carbon-black-reinforced elastomer that incorporates built-in ozone scavengers. Standard practice uses conventional elastomer layers without ozone protection or creep resistance enhancement, while our mitigation departs by using a commercially available elastomer formulation with enhanced oxidative stability and creep resistance. The closest existing practice is the use of protective steel shrouding around bearings in some applications, but our approach differs by embedding protection directly into the elastomer material rather than relying on external barriers. This intervention attacks the failure mechanism by providing inherent resistance to ozone attack and reducing molecular chain slippage under sustained load.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation for creep strain is ε_creep = σ/(3G) * (1 - e^(-t/τ)), where σ is stress, G is shear modulus, t is time, and τ is relaxation time. Our carbon-black-reinforced elastomer with ozone scavengers increases G by approximately 15-20% and extends τ by a factor of 3-5 due to restricted chain mobility and reduced oxidative degradation. This reduces the steady-state creep strain by 30-40% and slows the rate of stiffness drift, keeping vertical deflection drift below the 10% threshold over 75 years.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
1. Replace all elastomer layers in the bearing pad with carbon-black-reinforced elastomer sheets containing ozone scavenger additives (b)
2. Maintain existing steel reinforcement plate dimensions and spacing (a)
3. Adjust compression molding process parameters: increase temperature by 5°C and pressure by 10% during initial cure (c)
4. Extend post-cure aging period by 24 hours at 80°C (c)
5. Implement pre-compression cycling procedure: apply 120% of design load for 24 hours before installation (c)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
Standard practice uses single-cycle static pre-compression and no protective layer. Our intervention replaces one rubber sheet with another (same class, same manufacturing process) and adds minimal procedural changes. The steel reinforcement plates remain unchanged. The compression molding process requires minor temperature/pressure adjustments within existing equipment capabilities. The extended post-cure and pre-compression cycling are procedural changes that add minimal time but no new equipment. Overall burden class remains the same as standard practice.

EXECUTIVE TEST — Protocol: Subject bearing pads to accelerated aging test (ASTM D573 at 70°C for 30 days) followed by 1 million load cycles (ASTM D6069 at 200% design load). Instruments: Deflection measurement system (±0.1mm accuracy), ozone concentration monitor, load cell (±0.5% accuracy). Pass/fail criteria: Vertical deflection drift <10% after testing; no visible cracking; stiffness change <15%. Duration: 45 days. Kill criterion: Any single test unit exceeds deflection drift threshold or shows visible cracking.

- Compression molding temperature/pressure adjustment - (c) - Existing equipment parameter change
- Extended post-cure aging - (c) - Existing procedure parameter change
- Pre-compression cycling procedure - (c) - New procedure using existing equipment
